newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian truck strike threatens aviation fuel supply.
newsitem.headline: Indian truck strike threatens aviation fuel supply.

text.p: Deliveries of aviation fuel to airports could well be affected by the national truck strike scheduled to start at midnight March 31, a spokesman for the All India Motor Transport Congress said.

The spokesman, a member of the national strike committee, said dock workers at Nava Shiva, the port for Bombay, would refuse to load or unload ships. The strike started a day earlier than first planned, at midnight on Sunday, in Maharashtra.
Speaking by telephone, he said aviation fuel was delivered by private carriers or government-owned tankers from companies such as Indian Oil. No airline officials were available to comment.

The spokesman, who is president of western India's Maharashtra federated union of trucks, tempos (mini trucks), tankers and buses, said the unions would not make special exceptions for perishables such as foods or day-old chicks which are shipped by air.
Most road transporters had stopped taking bookings and would not deliver to air cargo any shipments which arrived at their depots, he added.

Unions are protesting at a five per cent tax in the last Budget which would now class transporters as a service sector. They also object to increases of 300 to 400 percent in third party insurance that subsidiary companies of the government-owned General Insurance company are due to implement on April 1.

Political analysts in New Delhi say Finance Minister P. Chidambaram may find a way to defuse the strike by saying his budget's five per cent tax has yet to be finalised by Parliament. That could give him an escape route, they said.

There is a potential separate problem for air cargo in that April 1 is also the deadline for Air Traffic Controllers to opt in or out of a new terms of employment scheme with their current employer, the Airports Authority of India.
Air traffic sources say they understand that the Indian Air Force is gearing up its own air traffic personnel so they can step in if the civilian controllers take action.
